content.title: Preview: #6 Duke Blue Devils (0-0, 0-0 ACC) vs. Texas Longhorns (0-0, 0-0 SEC) - DukeBlog
content.text: The Blue Devils begin the season with a battle against Sean Miller and the Texas Longhorns in the inaugural Dick Vitale Invitational presented by Belk. ESPN in collaboration with the Charlotte Sports Foundation created this event that will annually honor Dick Vitale, the Hall of Fame broadcaster and one of the sport’s most iconic voices and ambassadors. Since joining ESPN during its first year in 1979, Vitale has called more than 1,000 games. His unmistakable passion and signature style have helped shape the college basketball experience for fans for more than four decades, while cementing his legacy as one of the most beloved and enduring figures in sports broadcasting history. Vitale’s countless accolades include induction into the Naismith Basketball and Sports Broadcasting Halls of Fame. Most recently, he received the prestigious Dean Smith Award from the U.S. Basketball Writers Association (USBWA), and was introduced by former ESPN President George Bodenheimer as The New York Athletic Club’s Winged Foot Award recipient. Broadcast Information TV/Video Stream ESPN Play-by-Play Dave O’Brien Analyst Jay Bilas Analyst Dick Vitale Sideline Kris Budden Radio Blue Devil Sports Net. Play-by-Play David Shumate Analyst John Roth Engineer John Rose In Durham 96.5 FM & 620 AM SiriusXM 106 or 193 & SiriusXM app The Coaches Duke Jon Scheyer (Duke ‘10) Career Record / at Duke 89-22 (4th) / same vs. Texas First meeting Texas Sean Miller (Pittsburgh ‘92) Career Record / at School 437-196 (21st) / 0-0 (1st) vs. Duke 2-2 overall / 0-2 at Xavier / 2-0 at Arizona Texas Longhorns The Longhorns, last season, won 19 games against 16 losses, going 6-12 in conference and moved from their coach Rodney Terry after 2 seasons. Sean Miller was named head coach of Texas on March 24th, 2025. This is Sean Miller’s first season as head coach at the University of Texas. He’s spent his previous seasons coaching at Xavier and the University of Arizona. Texas returns a trio of productive guards from last year’s squad, including senior Jordan Pope, who was 3rd on last year’s team in scoring at 11 points per game. Tramon Mark, a 5th year senior responsible for 10.6 points per game and Chendall Weaver, another rising senior, responsible for 6.4 points and 4.9 rebounds last season. Miller also brought 2 players from his tenure at Xavier in forwards Dailyn Swain, a 6’8 guard who posted 8 points per game last season, and Lassina Traore who has career averages of (10.2 ppg) and 764 rebounds (8.8 rpg) among his 3 previous schools. Texas also received transfer commitments from Camden Heide, who as a Red shirt Sophomore at Purdue last season played in all 36 games (eight starts) and ranked third on the team in rebounding (3.6 rpg), fourth in minutes (19.6 mpg) and seventh in scoring (4.7 ppg). Matas Vokietaitis from FAU and Simeon Wilcher from St. John’s round out the transfer class for Sean Miller. Vokietaitis was named to the 2025 AAC All-Freshman Team while Wilcher started 27 games in his 2 seasons and averaged 5.7 points per game, where he averaged Also joining the Longhorns is a freshman class consisting of Declan Duru Jr. A 6’8 forward out of Germany, John Clark out of Houston, and Lewis Obiorah from London, England. Duke Blue Devils The Blue Devils are coming off of a 35-4 season that saw them within a game of a title shot. Duke went 19-1 in conference, winning both the regular season and the ACC Tournament. The Blue Devils welcome in a number 1 recruiting class after their Final Four run. Jon Scheyer after losing his entire starting lineup to the NBA but retaining core pieces with experience. Leading Duke are experienced returners senior big Maliq Brown and junior guard Caleb Foster, both instrumental pieces in Duke’s run this past season. Duke also returned 3 members from last season freshman class in hot shooting Isaiah Evans, who shot a team high 41.6%. Duke also brings back Darren Harris who has reshaped his body in hopes for a larger role and Patrick Ngongba who similarly has reshaped his frame, coming into this season healthy. Duke’s freshman class includes the Boozer brothers, Cayden and Cameron, do-it-all forward Nik Khamenia and Italian import Dame Sarr. Duke also added reserves Jack Scott and Ifeanyi Ufochukwu, from Princeton and Rice, respectively. Projected Starters Duke Blue Devils G Caleb Foster 6’4, 205lbs Jr. G Isaiah Evans 6’6, 180lbs So. G Dame Sarr 6’8, 190lbs Fr. F Cameron Boozer 6’9, 250lbs Fr. C Patrick Ngongba 6’11, 250lbs So. Texas Longhorns G Jordan Pope 6′ 1, 180lbs Sr. G Tramon Mark 6’5, 210lbs Gr. F Nic Codie 6’8, 220lbs So. F Dailyn Swain 6′ 8, 225 lbs. Jr. F Lassina Traore 6’9, 245lbs, RsSr. X-Factors The X factor for Duke is Nik Khamenia, he’s the prototype glue guy and jack-of-all-trades. He functions in Jon Schemer’s offense as a connector but is capable of having big offensive games either from an outside shooting aspect or as a driver to get to the free throw line. Defensively, he has the size to guard multiple positions. The X factor for Texas, Dailyn Swain, a transfer from Xavier really raises the ceiling for this Texas team, he’s a very versatile forward and one o the best athletes on the team. He rebounds the basketball well and gives Sean Miller a driver with a good handle on the wing. Final Thoughts We only have 2 exhibition games to really go on, but the early returns for the Blue Devils show a couple of areas of concern for Jon Scheyer’s team. The first area will be defensively, transition opportunities were en masse in those first two outings, which isn’t as concerning as Duke’s ability to locate in transition. Not wholly unexpected for a young team still learning each other and how to communicate, but it’s something the staff has had to make a point of emphasis. Defensive communication to begin games was an issue in general during those first two games so it’s an area for sure we all will be watching. Foul trouble, Duke has more depth on the wing than they do in the middle, and with Maliq Brown’s status unknown Duke has to find ways to keep Patrick Ngongba out of trouble – obviously Duke can shift Cam Boozer to the 5-spot but that definitely isn’t where Jon Scheyer wants to live if it can be helped. The game plan has to be to exert and steady themselves defensively to begin the game. The shots will fall eventually if they don’t immediately, but scoring and not defending is a war of attrition, Duke has to limit the effectiveness of the Texas offense to win – Jon Scheyer has built his version of this program with a defense first mantra. Again, Duke will face a much older team with a lot of weaponry and strength. Duke’s talent advantage only presents as an advantage if they are able to do the small things that lead to big results. Boxing out, guarding, being first to the ball. Related
